name: Guo Lianxue
current_role: Listed as CEO of Donglong Group (Shanghai Donglong Down Products Co., Ltd.), per a third-party company profile
profile: Guo Lianxue (郭连学) is associated with Shanghai Donglong, a down and textiles group founded in 1992 in Jinze Town, Qingpu District, Shanghai. The group makes down raw materials, home-textile fabrics, synthetic fillings, bedding and apparel. He appeared on the Hurun China list in 2008. There is very little recent public information about him.
interesting_fact: Donglong Group, founded in 1992, covers the down supply chain from raw down to finished bedding and garments. A third-party profile lists Guo Lianxue as CEO, while the legal representative of record is Guo Xiao.
notes: Low-profile private Chinese manufacturer with almost no English-language coverage. His role comes from a third-party aggregator (36Kr PitchHub) and may be out of date. I could not find an official company site or a published contact.

name: Padmakar Haribhau Mulay
current_role: Chairman, Ajeet Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (PM Group), Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra
profile: Padmakar Mulay founded Ajeet Seeds in Aurangabad in 1986 and built it into a hybrid-seed company covering 22 crops. It is the flagship of the PM Group, which also includes construction (Gangamai Industries & Construction), sugar and other seed businesses. His son Sameer Mulay runs it day to day as managing director.
interesting_fact: Ajeet Seeds' first big hit was the Ajeet-11 cotton hybrid, launched in 1992. The company says it was the first private seed company in India to introduce a proprietary wheat variety, Ajeet-102.
deep_cut_fact: Ajeet Seeds set up its own Plant Biotechnology Research Center in Hanumantgaon (Gangapur taluka) in 2003. Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University recognises it as a research centre, and it launched three Bt cotton hybrids in kharif 2006.
notes: Elder founder. A Feb 2025 Lokmat obituary of his brother lists him (as Padmakarrao Mulay) among the surviving brothers. MD Sameer Mulay is the public face of the company. The email is the company's general address, and the X account belongs to the company, not to him personally.

name: Delores B Weaver
current_role: Philanthropist; 10%+ shareholder of Shoe Station Group Inc. (formerly Shoe Carnival); namesake and backer of the Delores Barr Weaver Policy Center, Jacksonville
profile: Delores Barr Weaver is a Jacksonville philanthropist and former co-owner of the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars with her husband J. Wayne Weaver, the Shoe Carnival co-founder. Her stake in the retailer comes from that family holding; the company renamed itself Shoe Station Group (Nasdaq: SHOE) in June 2026. She has directed more than $100 million to causes in Northeast Florida.
interesting_fact: In July 2023 she gave $61 million to her donor-advised fund at the Community Foundation for Northeast Florida, the largest gift in the foundation's 60-year history. She has also endowed funds for more than four dozen local nonprofits.
deep_cut_fact: She was the first backer of a policy center devoted solely to girls in the juvenile justice system. The Delores Barr Weaver Policy Center opened in 2013 out of Jacksonville's 'Justice for Girls' movement and has served more than 4,000 girls and young women.
notes: She turned 90 in 2026, according to a post from the Policy Center. Her giving is administered through the Community Foundation for Northeast Florida (jaxcf.org), so the most respectful route is probably via the Policy Center or the Community Foundation. She is outspoken on social causes (see the Chronicle of Philanthropy profile). No personal contact is published.

name: Sridhar Vembu
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Zoho Corporation (stepped down as CEO in January 2025)
profile: Sridhar Vembu co-founded AdventNet with his brothers in 1996. It was renamed Zoho in 2009 and grew into a bootstrapped SaaS company with no outside investors. He has an IIT Madras degree and a Princeton PhD and started his career as a wireless engineer at Qualcomm. He handed the CEO role to Shailesh Davey in January 2025 to focus on R&D as Chief Scientist, and he runs Zoho's rural-development work from Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu.
interesting_fact: He moved from the Bay Area to the village of Mathalamparai in Tenkasi district in 2019, and Zoho set up offices there to bring product development to rural India. He received the Padma Shri in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004 he started Zoho Schools (originally Zoho University), which trains rural students in software as an alternative to college. Zoho says 15-20% of its engineers have no college degree.
notes: Very active on X (@svembu) and accessible to podcasters, especially on deep tech, rural R&D and Indian manufacturing; Zoho is also building chips and its own data-centre infrastructure. Hurun's figure is outdated: Forbes put Vembu and his siblings at about $6B in October 2025. Avoid personal topics, as his divorce litigation is public.

name: William J McMorrow
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Kennedy Wilson (taken private in June 2026 by a consortium he led with Fairfax Financial)
profile: Bill McMorrow, a former banker, bought the small real-estate auction firm Kennedy-Wilson in 1988, when it had one office and 11 employees. He grew it into a global real estate investor with about $16B of assets under management across the US, UK, Ireland, Spain and Japan. In June 2026 he and Fairfax completed a take-private at $10.90 a share. He keeps operational control while Fairfax holds the majority economic interest.
interesting_fact: He has taken three companies public in three countries: Kennedy-Wilson on the NYSE, Kennedy Wilson Japan in Tokyo, and Kennedy Wilson Europe Real Estate in London. The London company's $1.7B IPO was the second-largest real-estate IPO in the London Stock Exchange's 200-year history.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 17 years in banking before buying Kennedy-Wilson. That included eight years as a Senior VP at Fidelity Bank in Pennsylvania, followed by EVP and chair of the Credit Policy Committee at Imperial Bank in Los Angeles. In 2011 Kennedy Wilson led the recapitalisation of Bank of Ireland, which was its entry into Europe.
notes: The company is now private, so the SEC-derived net worth is out of date: he cashed out or rolled over his stake in the take-private. The best route is Emily Heidt, MD Communications, the media contact on the June 2026 release; she is a company contact, not his personal one. His bio page also has an 'Open contact form' link. He has appeared on podcasts (ceointerviews.ai lists interviews).

name: C Selvam
current_role: Whole-time Director, Asvini Fisheries Pvt. Ltd., Chennai, per company-registry aggregators (likely Chandrasekaran Selvam)
profile: C Selvam is linked to Asvini Fisheries, a Chennai seafood processor and exporter incorporated in 1986 that runs a raw-fish freezing unit at Tuticorin. Registry data lists Chandrasekaran Selvam as whole-time director since 1994. He is also a director of Asvini Hatcheries, Selvam Exports, Emerald Fishing and Meridian Fisheries, and is listed on the Seafood Exporters Association of India.
interesting_fact: His directorships cover much of the seafood chain: hatcheries (Asvini Hatcheries), fishing (Emerald Fishing Co.), processing and exports (Asvini Fisheries, Selvam Exports).
notes: Very low public profile. The identity rests only on registry aggregators (Tofler/Qorpiq) matching 'C Selvam' to Chandrasekaran Selvam at Asvini Fisheries; this is plausible but not confirmed by a primary source. I found no company website or published contact. The search budget ran out before a fuller check.

name: Manoj Agarwalla
current_role: Director and shareholder, Dhansar Engineering Company Pvt. Ltd. (per Tofler registry listing)
profile: Manoj Agarwalla is a director of Dhansar Engineering, a family mining contractor incorporated in 1955. It does overburden removal, coal extraction, drilling and blasting, and coal transport, mainly in the Dhanbad coalfield. Harsh Agarwalla is also listed as a director. The firm wins large hiring contracts from Coal India's Bharat Coking Coal Ltd (BCCL).
interesting_fact: Dhansar Engineering dates back to 1955 and does open-cast mining work: site levelling, overburden removal, drilling and blasting, coal extraction, wagon loading and transport. A BCCL award notice reported in search results gave it a roughly Rs 64.5 crore, 36-month contract in the Kustore area.
notes: Do not confuse him with Manoj Kumar Agarwal, CMD of BCCL since Sept 2025, who is a different person. The identity link rests on the Tofler registry listing, and I found no company website or published contact. Relevant to the energy (coal) theme, but very private. I could not open the BCCL contract PDF to verify the Rs 64.5 crore figure (bcclweb.in was unreachable), so treat it as unverified.

name: Matthew B. Oppenheimer
current_role: Co-founder and board director, Remitly Global (Nasdaq: RELY); former CEO. Sebastian Gunningham is CEO as of 2026.
profile: Matt Oppenheimer co-founded Remitly in Seattle in 2011 with Josh Hug and Shivaas Gulati and ran it as CEO for more than a decade, through its 2021 IPO. Remitly is a mobile-first cross-border payments company with more than 9.6 million customers. By 2026 Sebastian Gunningham had taken over as CEO and Oppenheimer remained on the board.
interesting_fact: In 2025, while still CEO, he spoke at the Milken Institute Global Conference and the Philadelphia Fed fintech conference about widening access to financial services for immigrants who send money home.
deep_cut_fact: Remitly did not start under that name. It began in 2011 as BeamIt Mobile, a search engine for comparing remittance services, before it started moving money itself, and it was renamed Remitly in August 2012.
notes: I could not confirm the exact date of the CEO handover or his current title beyond director: the SEC data says Director, and Remitly's Sept 2026 release names Gunningham as CEO. Check the Remitly IR site (blocked to my fetcher) before outreach. The widely told founding story about his time at Barclays in Kenya is not verified here. He has a LinkedIn profile, but I did not verify the URL.

name: Jagdeep Singh
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO/Chairman of QuantumScape; retired from the board at the end of 2024. I could not verify a current role.
profile: Jagdeep Singh is a serial deep-tech founder. He founded and ran optical-networking company Infinera as CEO from 2001 to 2009, then co-founded solid-state battery maker QuantumScape in 2010 with Tim Holme and Stanford professor Fritz Prinz. He was CEO until February 2024, when Siva Sivaram took over after a year-long succession plan, and he left the chairmanship and board at the end of 2024.
interesting_fact: He planned his own exit: QuantumScape's 8-K says Siva Sivaram's appointment as CEO in Feb 2024 was the culmination of a year-long succession plan that Singh started as chairman and outgoing CEO. Before that he had led the company since founding it in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He has three degrees from three schools: a B.S. in computer science from the University of Maryland, an M.S. in computer science from Stanford, and an MBA from UC Berkeley Haas. He also sat on the boards of the SPACs Khosla Ventures Acquisition Co. and Slam Corp. in 2021-22.
notes: A strong fit for the energy theme (batteries). He started the QuantumScape CEO succession himself, so it was not an ouster. The SEC net-worth figure dates from 2024, before his equity awards terminated when he retired. I found no personal site or published contact; LinkedIn is the likely route but I did not verify it.

name: Nguyen Duc Tai
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mobile World Investment Corporation (MWG; Thegioididong, Dien May Xanh, Bach Hoa Xanh)
profile: Nguyễn Đức Tài (born 1969, Nam Định) studied finance and accounting at the University of Economics HCMC and earned an MBA from the French-Vietnamese CFVG programme. In 2004 he and four partners founded Thegioididong, which grew into MWG, Vietnam's largest electronics and phone retailer, with the Bach Hoa Xanh grocery chain and the EraBlue venture in Indonesia. He was CEO until 2019 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: MWG started in March 2004 as a basic e-commerce site that only displayed product information, backed by three tiny shops on Hoàng Văn Thụ street in HCMC. It became profitable after moving to a bigger store on Nguyễn Đình Chiểu that October.
deep_cut_fact: Thegioididong had five co-founders, not one: Tài, Trần Lê Quân, Đinh Anh Huân, Điêu Chính Hải Triều and Trần Huy Thanh Tùng. Before founding it, Tài had trained in finance and accounting and earned a French-Vietnamese (CFVG) MBA.
notes: The $96M Wikidata net-worth figure probably understates his MWG holding. He is well known in Vietnam for blunt speeches at MWG shareholder meetings. Outreach in Vietnamese via MWG IR is the most practical route; I found no personal contact. The search budget ran out, so I could not find an English-language deep cut.

name: Steven Sell
current_role: Former President and CEO of agilon health (2020 to Aug 2025); advisor to early-stage healthcare companies. I could not verify a current role.
profile: Steven J. Sell is a managed-care executive. He ran Health Net's Western Region from 2008 to 2016 and was President, CEO and Chairman of Health Net from 2016 to 2019, the period of its sale to Centene. He led value-based primary-care company agilon health from 2020 through its 2021 IPO, then stepped down as CEO and director in August 2025, when co-founder Ron Williams became Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: agilon health, which he led for five years, partners with independent primary-care physician groups to move them into full-risk Medicare Advantage contracts, a model built around doctors rather than insurers.
deep_cut_fact: He is a liberal-arts graduate (B.A. from Swarthmore College) who went on to a Stanford GSB MBA. While running agilon he also advised several early-stage healthcare startups.
notes: He is no longer at agilon, so the agilon press (media@agilonhealth.com) and IR contacts no longer reach him. The SEC net-worth figure reflects 2025 holdings and the stock has fallen sharply, so it is likely overstated. His exit came alongside withdrawn guidance, so avoid making that the angle. LinkedIn is the probable route, but I did not verify it. Not a natural fit for the energy/data-center theme.
